Subject: Recap + next steps: token profile & pricing options for BrightHealth AI

Hi Marta / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a concrete ask to help us model pricing:

Call highlights
- Primary use: personalized member outreach + summarization of clinical notes + searching long member histories for care insights.
- Expected peak: 350–500 requests/min during daytime windows; typical steady-state much lower.
- Integrations: internal EHR extracts (PII), will need VPC/private deployment for production.

Data we need to finalize a proposal
- Typical (avg) prompt tokens per request (including system/prompt + context)
- Avg completion tokens generated per request
- Proportion of requests that require extended context (8k vs 32k vs 128k)
- Monthly token range (min/expected/max) and target $/1M tokens you are budgeting for

Provisional next steps
1) Marta to share sampled prompt/completion stats (we can accept CSV or JSONL with 50–200 samples).
2) We will return 3 pricing scenarios (pilot, production, enterprise) that show unit economics (effective $/1M tokens) and the premium for larger context lengths.
3) If numbers look good, schedule a short technical validation week and a pilot (30–60 days).

I attached a small prompt_samples.jsonl template and will send scenario pricing by EOD tomorrow once we get your averages.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Laura —

Thanks for the recap. Below are the numbers pulled from our staging logs (sample of last 30 days). Happy to share a small CSV of raw samples as well.

High-level token stats (per request averages)
- Avg prompt tokens (system + user + retrieved context): 480 tokens
- Avg completion tokens (model output): 1,120 tokens
- Median prompt: 320 tokens; median completion: 600 tokens

Context-length mix (estimated share of requests)
- 8k context: ~80% (most member lookups and short summaries)
- 32k context: ~15% (longer history summarization / multi-visit aggregation)
- 128k context: ~5% (rare, batch retrievals for complex care coordination)

Monthly volumes (expected)
- Min: 0.6M tokens/month
- Expected: 6.5M tokens/month
- Max (seasonal peaks): 22M tokens/month

Budget target
- We are targeting roughly $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens (effective) initially; willing to consider discounts for committed volume and a reserved capacity option.

Compliance ask
- We need a basic SOC 2 summary and an inventory of where KV cache / context snapshots are stored before moving to a private deployment. I attached a short security request doc.

Let me know if you want the raw CSV; we can scrub PII and share 200 sample rows.

—Marta

Marta —

Appreciate the numbers, that helps a lot. Attached two things: pricing_scenarios.csv (3 scenarios) and a small prompt sample template we used for estimation. Below are the headline economics and assumptions so we can align quickly.

Assumptions- Model: open-llm-32k-compatible (we’ll show hosted and private pricing)
- Avg prompt / completion per your numbers: prompt=480, completion=1,120
- Request distribution per your mix: 80%/15%/5% for 8k/32k/128k

Scenario A — Pilot (no commit)
- Provision: shared hosted, no SLA
- Price guidance: $1,100 per 1M tokens (baseline per-token rate)
- Expected monthly cost at 6.5M tokens: ~$7,150

Scenario B — Production (3–6 month commit)
- Provision: reserved capacity (dedicated pool), can include KV caching for repeated lookups
- Negotiated rate: $800 per 1M tokens (= ~27% discount)
- Additional 32k context premium: +12% on per-token for requests using 32k; 128k requests: +30%
- Expected monthly cost at 6.5M tokens (mix applied): ~$5,360

Scenario C — Enterprise (12 month commit + Private deployment)
- Provision: private VPC + extended support and audit logs
- Negotiated rate: $500 per 1M tokens (volume + commitment)
- 32k premium: +8%; 128k premium: +20%
- Expected monthly cost at 6.5M tokens (mix applied): ~$3,650

Notes on unit economics and how context affects cost
- Base per-token rate reflects steady-state inference (continuous batching + KV cache).
- 32k/128k contexts have higher memory and throughput cost; we apply a context-length premium rather than a flat multiplier for all tokens to keep short-context ops efficient.
- We can reduce effective cost by: prefix caching, summarization to shorten input context, and request-level sampling to avoid generating full-length completions when not needed.

Requested confirmation
- Which scenario(s) should we model as a formal quote? (A/B/C)
- Would you like us to simulate the monthly cost if we change avg completion from 1,120 to 700 tokens (tight summary setting)?

Next steps
- If you confirm scenario B or C, we’ll produce a draft contract and a proposed reserved capacity configuration.
- We’ll also schedule a technical sync with Rishi (cc’d) next week to walk through KV caching and private deployment network requirements.

Link to draft pricing scenarios (private drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pricing-samples

Thanks —
Laura
(Account Executive, Redwood Inference)
